title: Reachability
ports.title: Ports players need
bind.all: Published on every interface of this host ({{address}}).
bind.loopback: Bound to {{address}}: not reachable from outside by design — for a tunnel or a proxy on this host. No port needs to be opened.
bind.private: Published only on {{address}}, a local network address: the router has to forward the ports to exactly this address.
bind.public: Published only on {{address}}, an internet address of this host.
public.none: No public address is set, so players do not know where to connect and nothing can be checked from outside.
public.server: Players connect to {{host}} (set on this server).
public.installation: Players connect to {{host}} (the installation's public address).
public.private: The public address {{host}} is a local or reserved address: players on the internet cannot use it.
firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.docker: Docker bypasses ufw: a published port is forwarded by Docker's own rules before ufw sees it, so "ufw allow" neither opens nor closes it. Filter in Docker's DOCKER-USER chain or in the host's forward chain instead.
firewall.hint.iptables: Needed only if your DOCKER-USER chain drops traffic. One line each for IPv4 and IPv6. The rules are gone after a reboot unless you save them (e.g. netfilter-persistent save).
firewall.hint.nftables: For a host ruleset whose forward chain has policy drop. Adjust table and chain to your ruleset, and put the rule into /etc/nftables.conf to keep it.
firewall.hint.ufw: Only has an effect where ufw filters forwarded container traffic (the ufw-docker setup). With a plain ufw, Docker's published ports are open regardless of these rules.
router.title: Router and cloud firewall
router.forward: At home: forward every port above on the router to this host's local address — the same number outside and inside, with the protocol shown. Not needed on a server with its own internet address.
router.cgnat: If the router's internet address starts with 100.64 to 100.127 (carrier-grade NAT) or differs from the address websites see, forwarding cannot work: ask the provider for a public IPv4 address, or run the server elsewhere.
router.cloud: Cloud servers often have a firewall in front of the host (AWS security groups, Google Cloud firewall rules, Azure network security groups, Oracle Cloud security lists and similar): allow the same ports and protocols there too.
inside.title: Check from inside
inside.text: Does Docker publish every port, and does the game answer? Asked from the dashboard; nothing leaves this host.
outside.title: Check from outside
outside.off: Switched off. This check asks third-party services to look at the server from the internet. To offer it, set GSS_REACHABILITY_PROBES=on in the .env and restart the dashboard.
outside.sends.title: What is sent, and to whom
outside.sends.ip_port: the public IPv4 address and the game port
outside.sends.ip_ports: the public IPv4 address and the TCP ports
outside.sends.note: A DNS name is resolved on this host, only the address is sent. No key, no server name, no password. Answers are reused for {{seconds}} s.
outside.plan.steam: {{name}}: is the server listed at this address?
outside.plan.mcstatus: {{name}}: Minecraft status ping from the internet
outside.plan.none: Not checkable from outside (UDP without a service that speaks the game's protocol).
